post.description: On a stopped instance it's synchronous: the volume takes the instance's next free volume slot and the guest sees it at the next start. The volume must be available and in the instance's project. On a running instance it's asynchronous: 202 with an AttachVolume operation, and the guest sees the disk once it succeeds (409 instance_restart_required until the instance is stopped and started once; 503 actions_unavailable while its control plane is unavailable). Attaching a volume that's already attached answers 200, or 202 with the attach's open operation.

post.description: On a stopped instance it's synchronous and the volume becomes available. The root volume can't be detached (409 root_volume). On a running instance it's asynchronous: 202 with a DetachVolume operation, which waits for the guest to release the disk; force frees the volume without the guest (the guest sees I/O errors on it and may lose writes it hadn't made). A repeat answers the open operation, and a repeat with force escalates it. 409 volume_detaching while a force-detached disk is still in the guest.
